answer: An agent marketplace requires every bidding identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days, with the bond forfeited if a verifiable fraud proof succeeds. Each identity is an island of locked collateral: the same dollar cannot back two accounts. Creating 10,000 identities therefore ties up $1 million and exposes it to slashing. Cheap account creation offers no haven from this rule, even in a gale of automated signups.
